sec13-card-sec13-F05.expected_back: Three-year records release under privacy law through licensed operators, the agency website, or mailed requests naming full name, birth date, and license number, cost twenty-five dollars, and run free past age sixty-five.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.front: What is the standard price of a three-year driving record, and which age group pays nothing?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.expected_back: Three-year histories cost twenty-five dollars and run free past sixty-five.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.front: Who gets called into a compliance hearing or medical review, what do safety courses teach, and what if habits stay unsafe?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.expected_back: Careless, lawless, substance-troubled, or otherwise unsafe drivers face compliance hearings where the division teaches self-improvement and safer technique, medically limited drivers need division approval under doctor-committee standards, safety courses drill instruction, counseling, defensive technique, trap-spotting, risk-cutting, and attitude, and unimproved drivers lose privileges for everyone's safety.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.front: What is the goal of a driver compliance hearing, and what happens when a driver fails to improve?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.expected_back: Hearings retrain unsafe and unwell drivers, and failures forfeit privileges.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.front: How does Oklahoma classify every driver license held under age eighteen, and how many moving violations can trigger suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.expected_back: Under-eighteen licenses run probationary on a safe-legal trial with discretionary cancellation or suspension for any moving violation.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.front: Why must drivers under eighteen treat their license like an active trial period?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.expected_back: Junior licenses trial safe-legal driving with hair-trigger suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.front: Which seven serious conviction categories trigger mandatory Oklahoma revocation, and what is the revocation window?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.expected_back: Convictions mandatorily revoke privileges six months to three years for vehicular manslaughter or negligent homicide, intoxicated driving or control without double-counting same-incident consent revocations, vehicle-aided felonies, death-or-injury hit-and-runs, license or vehicle perjury and false oaths, vehicle-linked drug convictions of any grade, and under-twenty-one measurable-alcohol driving or control.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.front: How long do Oklahoma's seven mandatory-revocation offenses pull privileges, and how are same-incident alcohol revocations handled?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.expected_back: Seven conviction families revoke six months to three years without same-incident doubling.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.front: Where does every driver's point balance start, and what point total within what timeframe triggers suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.expected_back: The mandatory point system opens everyone clean, scores one or more points per pointable conviction, suspends at ten points within five years, and allows reductions.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.front: What cumulative score and lookback window suspend an Oklahoma license under the point system?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.expected_back: Clean slates suspend at ten points inside five years.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.front: Which violations add four, three, two, or one point on Oklahoma's point schedule?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.expected_back: Pointable convictions assess four points for reckless driving or failing to stop or stay stopped for a loading or unloading school bus, three points for exceeding the posted speed limit by more than twenty-five miles per hour, two points for restriction violations, careless driving, speeding, following too closely, disobeying a stop sign or traffic signal, failing to yield, or driving left of center or the wrong way on a one-way road, and one point for a defective vehicle or any other violation excluding offenses requiring suspension or revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.front: Which two violations sit at the four-point top of the point chart, and which sit at the one-point bottom?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.expected_back: Reckless driving and failing to stop or remain stopped for a loading or unloading school bus carry four points, while operating a defective vehicle and all other violations except those requiring suspension or revocation carry one point.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.front: How do clean twelve-month stretches, three clean years, and defensive-driving courses reduce your Oklahoma point total?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.expected_back: Clean twelve-month stretches erase two points, three clean years zero the total, approved compliance or defensive courses erase two points once per twenty-four months, and totals never drop below zero.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.front: Which two paths subtract points from your driving record, and why can't you bank negative points?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.expected_back: Clean years and courses shave twos off totals floored at zero.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.front: What are Oklahoma's mandatory liability insurance minimums, who can demand proof, and what penalties hit uninsured drivers?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.expected_back: Compulsory liability minimums repeat at twenty-five thousand dollars per person, fifty thousand per multi-victim crash, and twenty-five thousand property per accident with proof owed officers, agency representatives, and fellow crash parties on demand, stale addresses risk unknowing suspension, uninsured convictions draw up to two hundred fifty dollars, thirty days in jail, or both plus license and registration suspension, and testing sites span the state with locations posted online.

sec13-card-sec13-R12.front: Which four reminders wrap up Oklahoma's compulsory insurance and licensing chapter?
sec13-card-sec13-R12.expected_back: Minimums repeat, addresses stay current, uninsured convictions fine-plus-jail-plus-suspend, and test sites span the state.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.front: What three vehicle credentials belong with a driven Oklahoma car, where do you handle them, and what sets title-transfer fees?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.expected_back: Driven cars need a current tag, registration, and title, registration at a Service Oklahoma site or licensed operator after taxes and fees buys a new tag or year sticker, buyers and sellers must transfer title there to prove ownership, and transfer fees follow vehicle age, type, and value.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.front: How does what vehicle registration proves differ from what a title transfer proves?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.expected_back: Registration buys the tag or sticker proving taxes paid, while title transfer proves ownership changes hands at sale.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.front: Where does Service Oklahoma mail every official notice, and how can an outdated address cost your license?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.expected_back: Every Service Oklahoma letter goes to your address of record, so a stale address can suspend you without your ever knowing, and keeping the license means keeping in touch.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.front: Why does failing to update your Service Oklahoma mailing address create a hidden suspension hazard?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.expected_back: Mail follows the address of record only, so stale records can suspend you in ignorance.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.front: What does vehicle liability mean, and what three dollar minimums per accident does the Oklahoma manual print?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.expected_back: Liability means legal and financial responsibility for collision injury, death, or property damage caused by you or your vehicle, and the manual prints Oklahoma's per-accident minimums as twenty-five thousand dollars for injury or death of two or more persons, fifty thousand dollars for injury or death of two or more persons, and twenty-five thousand dollars for property damage.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.front: How are all three of Oklahoma's printed $25,000 / $50,000 / $25,000 compulsory liability minimums measured?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.expected_back: On the compulsory insurance page, Oklahoma's minimum limits are printed as twenty-five thousand dollars for injury or death of two or more persons, fifty thousand dollars for injury or death of two or more persons, and twenty-five thousand dollars of property damage, with all minimum limits counted per accident.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.front: What insurance form must stay in your car, who can demand to inspect it, and what three details should you copy after a crash?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.expected_back: Show a current security verification form at any collision or traffic stop as supplied by the owner insurer or a non-owner policy, keep it in the car, display it to officers, Service Oklahoma staff, and fellow crash parties on demand, and copy the other side full name, license number, and birth dates for your own protection.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.front: Which three groups have the right to see your insurance verification form, and what do you record at a collision?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.expected_back: Officers, Service Oklahoma staff, and fellow crash parties all rate a look at your proof, and you copy their details in return.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.front: What injury or dollar-damage threshold suspends uninsured crash drivers and owners, and what does a court-reported no-proof ticket suspend?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.expected_back: Uninsured drivers and owners in a crash with any injury or five hundred dollars or more of damage lose the license to suspension, and a no-proof ticket pushes courts to notify Service Oklahoma for license plus tag suspension.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.front: How does the suspension triggered by an uninsured crash differ from a court-reported no-proof traffic ticket?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.expected_back: Uninsured crashes with injury or five-hundred-dollar damage suspend the license directly, while no-proof tickets suspend license plus tags through court notice.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.front: What fine, jail time, and credential losses follow a conviction for driving uninsured or refusing to show proof?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.expected_back: Conviction for ignoring compulsory insurance or withholding proof from an officer or Service Oklahoma representative draws up to two hundred fifty dollars, thirty days in jail, or both, plus suspension of license and registration.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.front: How does Oklahoma classify forging a security verification form versus merely possessing a fake one, and whose forms count?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.expected_back: Forging a security verification form risks felony conviction with fines and imprisonment, merely holding one risks a misdemeanor carrying up to two hundred fifty dollars plus mandatory suspension of driving privilege and registration, only insurer or agent issued forms count, and wise drivers confirm a current form in every car they touch since uninsured operation invites arrest and suspension.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.front: What criminal grade separates manufacturing a fake Oklahoma insurance form from simply keeping one in your glovebox?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.expected_back: Manufacturing a fake form is a felony, while merely possessing one is a misdemeanor pairing two hundred fifty dollars with mandatory suspension.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.front: Which occupants must wear federally approved factory seat belts in Oklahoma, and how do belts protect them?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.expected_back: Drivers and front passengers must buckle factory belts meeting federal standards, since belts soften interior impact, hold you inside and in control, and keep buckled riders from flying forward or out.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.front: What three physical crash protections do fastened seat belts deliver to riders?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.memory_hook: Cushion hits, hold control, prevent flight
sec03-card-sec03-R07.expected_back: Belts soften impact, pin riders inside and in command, and spare buckled passengers from forward flight.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.front: What restraint rules govern Oklahoma children under 2, under 8, and aged 4 to 8 up to 4 feet 9 inches?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.expected_back: Children under eight ride only in a proper child restraint, kids at least four stay secured, restraints face rearward until age two or the maker weight and height caps, every system must meet federal crash standards, and four to eight year olds no taller than four feet nine inches use a restraint or a seat belt.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.front: How do Oklahoma's child-restraint rules shift across age 2, ages 4 to 8, and height 4 feet 9 inches?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.expected_back: Rear-facing holds until age two or maker caps, under-eight means restrained, and four-to-eight at or under four-nine takes a restraint or a belt.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.front: Why must children never ride loose or in front of airbags, who belongs in back, and how much safer is the rear seat?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.expected_back: Never let a child ride loose, standing, or on the floorboards, no front-seat adult can stop an infant from windshield flight, airbags have killed sub-five-foot children and elders so under-twelves belong in back, the rear seat runs twenty-six percent safer, families should settle back-seat rules at home, and buckling up is the law.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.front: Why does holding a baby in an adult's arms or letting kids stand on seats or floorboards turn deadly?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.expected_back: No adult grip can save an unrestrained infant from windshield flight, and standing or floorboard riding invites skull injury.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.front: Which two groups under 5 feet tall have suffered fatal airbag injuries, where should under-12s sit, and what is the rear-seat safety gain?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.expected_back: Airbag force has killed children and older adults under five feet tall; when a vehicle has a passenger-side airbag, the Highway Safety Administration recommends seating children under twelve in back, and even without airbags the back seat is at least twenty-six percent safer than the front.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.question_text: Who must hold an Oklahoma driver license and vehicle tag once living here, and which group may be exempt?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.teaching_text: Moving to Oklahoma requires both an Oklahoma card and state plates, with only military members and spouses eligible for exemption.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: What two things must newcomers holding out-of-state licenses get once becoming Oklahoma residents, and who stays exempt?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.teaching_text: Establishing residency triggers transferring both your driver card and vehicle plates unless military-and-spouse exemptions apply.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: Which four groups can drive legally in Oklahoma without getting an Oklahoma driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.teaching_text: Licensed sixteen-plus visitors, military families, nonresident college families, and pure farm-ranch tractor operators need no Oklahoma plastic.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.question_text: How does the license exemption for out-of-state college students differ from the exemption for farm tractor hands?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.teaching_text: Nonresident students still carry valid home-state plastic, whereas tractor operators working strictly on farms and ranches need no card at all.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.question_text: How must your name and name-change papers match at Service Oklahoma, which primary IDs count, and why do copies fail?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.teaching_text: Bringing a photocopy or notarized duplicate instead of a certified birth certificate, valid passport, or post-November-2007 Oklahoma card gets rejected.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.question_text: What document standard do Service Oklahoma counters enforce on identity proof, and which two copy types always fail?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.teaching_text: Even a notary stamp on a photocopy cannot substitute for a government-issued original or agency-certified record.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.question_text: What ID proof is needed to replace a card, renew past one year expired, or adopt a new legal name?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.teaching_text: Replacements and year-plus renewals need primary ID, while name updates demand a passport, court decree, marriage certificate, or paired common-law affidavit.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.question_text: Where must legal name changes be filed first, do titles print on cards, and what happens with visitors or filing receipts?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.teaching_text: Social Security records must match first, titles never print, and temporary visitors or mere immigration receipts earn zero license.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.question_text: Which agency must log your legal name change before Service Oklahoma updates your card, and what prefixes are left off?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.teaching_text: Skipping Social Security causes database mismatches at the counter, and honorifics or religious titles never appear on plastic.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.question_text: Can an immigration application receipt prove lawful presence in Oklahoma, and which non-citizens are ineligible for a license?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.teaching_text: Pending filing receipts carry zero legal weight at licensing counters, and non-resident visitors cannot obtain an Oklahoma card.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.question_text: What insurance, medical, Social Security, and driver-education items belong in your licensing visit?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.teaching_text: Your Social Security number stays unprinted on the card, while missing approved school, commercial, or parent-taught proof can add restrictions.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: Starting May 7, 2025, which four restricted federal places or flights require a REAL ID or passport?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: Standard non-compliant state cards stop clearing airport checkpoints, military gates, designated federal buildings, and nuclear sites after that date.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.question_text: On what exact calendar date did REAL ID or federal passport enforcement begin for domestic flights and bases?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.teaching_text: Travelers without the star-marked state card after that spring deadline must carry a valid passport or federal credential.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: At age 18, which vehicles require CDL Classes A–C, what training applies, and what rules govern the commercial learner permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.teaching_text: CDL permits require English literacy, registry training, a twenty-one-plus rated co-driver, fourteen days before skills, and cap attempts at three before monthly waits.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.question_text: At age 18, what vehicles does Class D cover, how soon can you road-check, and what happens after three failures?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.teaching_text: Adults need no driver-ed class and can road-check next business day after passing written, though three road failures force monthly waits or a thirty-day permit.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.question_text: For an 18-year-old applicant, how does CDL training compare with Class D training requirements?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.teaching_text: Commercial applicants must study the CDL manual and complete listed entry training, while adult Class D applicants skip coursework.
sec01-card-sec01-R07.must_match_memory_hook: CDL requires training, Class D none

visual_sync.text_span: CDL requires training, Class D none

sec01-card-sec01-R08.question_text: How do skills-check waiting periods and three-strike retry rules compare across CDL permits, Class D permits, and direct adult testing?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.teaching_text: CDL permits hold fourteen days and Class D permits thirty, while skipping a permit lets adults try next business day up to three times.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: How do ages 15, 16, and 16.5 interact with driver education, the 180-day permit, Work Zone Safe, and lifting intermediate caps?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.teaching_text: Driver education unlocks learner permits at fifteen, intermediate cards at sixteen instead of sixteen-and-a-half, and full clearance in six months instead of twelve.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.question_text: What three age or waiting shortcuts does completing approved driver education unlock for Oklahoma teens?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.teaching_text: Coursework gets you a permit at fifteen, intermediate privileges six months sooner at sixteen, and unrestricted status in half the wait.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.question_text: Who is Oklahoma parent-taught driver education designed for, can families rush it, and what exact classroom and driving hours apply?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.teaching_text: Approved correspondence vendors charge fees and let families pace lessons at home, yet shortcuts are banned below thirty study and fifty-five behind-the-wheel hours.

sec01-card-sec01-R13.question_text: What three rules govern fees, pacing, and required hours in an Oklahoma parent-taught driver-ed course?
sec01-card-sec01-R13.teaching_text: Families pay the course provider directly and work at their student's speed while logging every single required classroom and road hour.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.question_text: What driving window, passenger limit, exceptions, and conviction freeze govern Oklahoma graduated teen drivers, and what crash stat explains why?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.teaching_text: With a quarter of sixteen-year-olds crashing or getting ticketed in year one, convictions freeze your graduated stage for six extra months.

sec01-card-sec01-R14.question_text: How many non-household passengers may an Oklahoma graduated teen carry without a 21+ adult, and how long does a moving conviction freeze progress?
sec01-card-sec01-R14.teaching_text: Job shifts, classes, church events, or an older licensed passenger excuse curfew, while moving tickets stall upgrades half a year.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.question_text: How does adding a motorcycle endorsement differ from getting a motorcycle-only license at age 14 in cc limit, riding hours, and course rules?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.teaching_text: Fourteen- and fifteen-year-old riders stay capped at three hundred cubic centimeters between four-thirty a.m. and nine p.m. and must finish a certified rider course under eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.question_text: How does adding an M endorsement to an existing license compare with starting fresh on a motorcycle-only card at 14?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.teaching_text: Licensed drivers can attach an endorsement—often waiving tests via MSF—whereas fourteen-year-olds pass vision, written, bike manual, and skills from scratch.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.question_text: What daily solo riding hours and highway rules apply to 14–15 small-bike riders, and what course rule applies under 18?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.teaching_text: Night riding past nine p.m. and minimum-speed freeways stay off-limits until sixteen, and every rider under eighteen needs certified basic training.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.question_text: What helmet, supervision, restriction-9, 30-day hold, and parent rules govern a 14-year-old motorcycle permit, and who can get a state ID?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.teaching_text: Young permit riders wear helmets under watchful twenty-one-plus endorsed eyes with parent liability signed, while non-driving ID cards serve any age.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.question_text: What requirements clear a teen motorcycle learner permit compared with getting a non-driving Oklahoma ID card?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.teaching_text: Clearing a bike permit demands thirty supervised days, code-nine eligibility, and parent liability at fourteen-fifteen, whereas IDs require only identity, residency, and minor consent.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.question_text: Which three exams make up Class D testing, what does sitting for them cost, when do you pay, and does your SSN print?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.teaching_text: Service Oklahoma charges zero testing fee up front—you pay card fees only after passing to get a paper temporary while plastic mails.

sec01-card-sec01-R15.question_text: When does money change hands during Service Oklahoma Class D testing, and what credential do you drive home with?
sec01-card-sec01-R15.teaching_text: You owe nothing until every required exam is passed, walking out with a valid paper temporary until your permanent card arrives by mail.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.question_text: What topics does the Class D written check cover, can you request an oral sitting, and how long must you wait after failing?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.teaching_text: Missing passing score on traffic laws, safe driving, or alcohol-drug rules requires waiting at least one full day before retesting.

sec01-card-sec01-R16.question_text: Are oral versions of the Oklahoma written check available, and what minimum wait follows a failed attempt?
sec01-card-sec01-R16.teaching_text: Requesting spoken delivery accommodates reading needs, and a mandatory full-day gap gives missed handbook rules time to sink in.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.question_text: What car rules, passenger/pet bans, fee options, scored maneuvers, and slick-road cancellation rule govern the Oklahoma driving check?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.teaching_text: Leave pets and extra passengers home, bring your tagged insured car, and remember slick pavement cancels every road check.

sec01-card-sec01-R17.question_text: How do certified-instructor road checks compare in cost with Service Oklahoma sites, and what pavement condition cancels both?
sec01-card-sec01-R17.teaching_text: Approved driving-school examiners charge for convenience while state stations charge zero exam fee, yet wet or icy pavement halts either one.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.question_text: Across Oklahoma's requirements table, how do required exams vary for new drivers, teens, expired renewals, out-of-state transfers, and IDs?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.teaching_text: Renewals under three years expired skip all exams while past three years triggers all three, and valid out-of-state Class D holders usually take vision only.

sec01-card-sec01-R18.question_text: How does letting an Oklahoma license stay expired past three years change testing compared with a valid out-of-state transfer?
sec01-card-sec01-R18.teaching_text: Passing the three-year expiration cliff forces vision, written, and road retesting, whereas valid newcomers take vision with written and road waivable.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.question_text: What five mistakes fail the Oklahoma driving check, and what legal meaning does saying yes to the red-heart organ donor prompt carry?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.teaching_text: Point losses, violations, danger, crashes, or refusing a maneuver fail the check, while a printed red heart gives binding legal organ-recovery consent.

sec01-card-sec01-R19.question_text: What happens right after failing a road check, and how do yes versus no work on LifeShare organ-donor signup?
sec01-card-sec01-R19.teaching_text: Examiners review your specific mistakes and set a retest date, while donor signup stays voluntary with family discussion encouraged.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.question_text: Which discharge or military papers earn Oklahoma's free Veteran card logo, and what two deadlines bind relocating sex or violent offenders?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.teaching_text: Qualifying veterans add the flag logo at zero extra logo charge, while relocating offenders have ten days for Corrections and three days for local police.

sec01-card-sec01-R20.question_text: Does the Veteran card indicator add an extra fee, and how do Corrections versus local-police offender registration clocks compare?
sec01-card-sec01-R20.teaching_text: Normal card fees apply with zero surcharge for the Veteran mark, and missing the three-day police or ten-day Corrections clock risks jail.
sec01-card-sec01-R20.must_match_memory_hook: Zero logo fee, ten and three

visual_sync.text_span: Zero logo fee, ten and three

sec01-card-sec01-F21.question_text: To whom must you display your license, what does a 4-year Class D cost overall, what do retests or replacements cost, and who pays $0?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.teaching_text: Carry your card to show officers, judges, and crash parties, paying four plus thirty-eight fifty—forty-two fifty total—while drivers sixty-five-plus pay nothing.

sec01-card-sec01-R21.question_text: What primary-ID habit applies to every card transaction, and how does the 4-year Class D price change at age 65?
sec01-card-sec01-R21.teaching_text: Originals, renewals, and twenty-five-dollar replacements all check primary ID, and reaching sixty-five waives the forty-two-fifty Class D fee completely.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.question_text: What third-brake-light years, windshield-tint band, tire-tread floor, horn distance, and door/mirror/insurance rules appear on Oklahoma's pre-test vehicle list?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.teaching_text: Examiners turn away cars with taped lenses, tint below five inches or the AS-one line, tread at or under two thirty-seconds, or missing driver insurance.

sec01-card-sec01-R22.question_text: Which ten equipment and paperwork areas get checked before your car can roll out on an Oklahoma road check?
sec01-card-sec01-R22.teaching_text: One broken door handle, taped brake lens, bald tire, silent horn, or insurance card omitting the test driver cancels your run before shifting into drive.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.question_text: Who legally owns your physical Oklahoma driver license card, what four actions can the state take against it, and when must you carry it?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.teaching_text: Paying fees and passing exams earns conditional driving privileges—never ownership of a card Oklahoma can suspend or revoke for violations.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.question_text: How does legal ownership of the license card separate from the driving privilege it represents?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.teaching_text: Understanding that driving is a revocable privilege rather than an untouchable property right explains why traffic courts can pull cards.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.question_text: Through which three channels can you replace a lost, destroyed, or unreadable Oklahoma card, and what status must your license hold?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.teaching_text: Suspended, revoked, or expired credentials cannot sneak back onto the road through a duplicate replacement order.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.question_text: What two term lengths are offered on Oklahoma licenses, on what day of which month do they expire, and how early can you renew?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.teaching_text: Your expiration locks to the final calendar day of the month you originally paid fees—not necessarily your birth month—with renewal open twelve months ahead.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.question_text: Which month anchors an Oklahoma license's 4- or 8-year term, and how far ahead does the renewal window open?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.teaching_text: Permit questions love catching drivers who assume Oklahoma cards expire on birthdays rather than the end of their fee-payment month.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.question_text: Where must temporary non-citizens process license visits, how are their expiration dates set, and how do permanent residents differ?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.teaching_text: Temporary status holders bring full immigration paperwork to a Service Oklahoma examiner every visit, whereas green-card holders can use any renewal site.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.question_text: What document rule and expiration tie apply to non-citizens versus lawful permanent residents at renewal?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.teaching_text: Forgetting even one supporting immigration document stalls non-citizen renewals at examiner desks, unlike permanent residents showing a valid green card.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.question_text: How can standard renewals be filed, what grace do out-of-state military members get on return, and what does a 1-year lapse force?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.teaching_text: Deployed troops get mail options or sixty days back home, whereas civilians expired past twelve months must bring a birth certificate or passport in person.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.question_text: How does Oklahoma treat returning military personnel compared with civilians whose licenses expired more than a year ago?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.teaching_text: Service members stationed away enjoy a sixty-day homecoming buffer, while year-late civilians lose online convenience and bring primary proof in person.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.question_text: Within how many days and by what three methods must movers notify Service Oklahoma, what do name changes require, and what risk do old addresses carry?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.teaching_text: Missing a mailed court or agency letter sent to your old apartment can suspend your license without you ever seeing a warning.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.question_text: How do the filing options for an Oklahoma address change differ from a legal name change, and why do stale addresses hurt?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.teaching_text: Moves update easily online, by operator, or via Box eleven-four-fifteen within ten days, whereas name updates need certified marriage or court documents.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.question_text: Until what birthday is every Oklahoma driver license probationary, and what three kinds of conduct can cancel or suspend it?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.teaching_text: Before your eighteenth birthday, any unlawful act, careless negligence, or behind-the-wheel misconduct gives Service Oklahoma authority to pull your card.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.question_text: What three categories of driving behavior can end a probationary under-18 Oklahoma license?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.teaching_text: Teen licenses operate on trial status until eighteen, meaning poor judgment behind the wheel costs privileges far faster than adult points.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.question_text: Does sitting beside a licensed adult legalize driving without a permit, and who else breaks the law by allowing an unlicensed driver?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.teaching_text: Without a valid learner permit or license in hand, both the person steering and the parent or car owner who allowed it face arrest.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.question_text: Why does putting a licensed friend or parent in the passenger seat fail to protect an unlicensed driver or vehicle owner?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.teaching_text: Supervised practice is legal only after earning a learner permit—lending keys to someone with zero credential violates Oklahoma law for both parties.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.question_text: What do license restriction codes represent, what can letter A mark on qualified rigs, and what max penalty hits unlicensed or restriction violations?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.teaching_text: Ignoring a required restriction code carries the exact same misdemeanor ceiling as driving unlicensed—up to five hundred dollars and six months jailed.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.question_text: How does Oklahoma punish violating a license restriction compared with driving completely unlicensed?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.teaching_text: Driving without required glasses or an adult companion legally voids your conditional privilege, triggering the same fine and jail range.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.question_text: What specific driver or vehicle adaptations do Oklahoma restriction codes B, F, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 require?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.teaching_text: From B corrective lenses and F left mirrors to code-four automatic shifters and code-six insulin snacks within reach, every code tailors safe control.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.question_text: How do letter codes B and F differ in focus from numbered codes 2 through 8 on an Oklahoma license?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.teaching_text: B and F address sight and left-side hearing with lenses or mirrors, while two through eight cover shifters, steering, insulin food, and prosthetics.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.question_text: How does Restriction 9 govern learner companions, and what cc, hour, passenger, speed, and helmet rules pack into Restriction 0?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.teaching_text: Code nine requires a twenty-one-plus front supervisor, while code zero restricts sub-sixteen riders to solo daylight three-hundred-cc trips—and thirty-five max under one-fifty cc.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.question_text: Who rides up front under Code 9, when do Code 0 engine and hour caps lift, and when does the helmet rule finally end?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.teaching_text: Turning sixteen drops Code zero's engine and curfew limits, yet Oklahoma's mandatory motorcycle helmet rule stays locked until age eighteen.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.question_text: What do Restrictions A and T signify on teen cards, when does T end, and how do you remove old codes or add endorsements?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.teaching_text: Restriction A covers supervised motorcycle learners, T enforces five-to-ten curfews and one-peer caps below eighteen, and an examiner clears outdated codes.

sec02-card-sec02-R11.question_text: How does clearing an outdated license restriction differ from adding a brand-new endorsement?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.teaching_text: Dropping an obsolete restriction takes an examiner review alone, whereas adding new vehicle privileges requires passing the matching exams too.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.question_text: Why do uniform road-sign shapes and colors matter—for instance on a damaged red octagon or any rectangular panel?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.teaching_text: Even bent or mud-splashed, a red eight-sided outline still commands a stop and a rectangle always states a rule or guide.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.question_text: What job do rectangular panels perform, and how do red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and brown divide meanings?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.teaching_text: Rectangles post binding rules like speed limits, while color separates red bans, orange roadwork, yellow warnings, and green-blue-brown guidance.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.question_text: What specific roadway meaning belongs to red, orange, yellow, fluorescent yellow-green, black-and-white, green, blue, and brown?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.teaching_text: Memorizing each color—especially neon yellow-green for schools, walkers, and bikes—tells you what lies ahead before reading a word.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.question_text: How does Oklahoma punish blocking or damaging a traffic sign normally versus when someone gets hurt or killed?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.teaching_text: Knocking down or covering a stop sign jumps from a misdemeanor to a two-year, thousand-dollar felony if a crash injures or kills anyone.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.question_text: What exact actions do stop octagons, 4-way/all-way plaques, red-white yield triangles, and red slashed rings command?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.teaching_text: Stop signs demand halting before marked or unmarked crosswalks, all-way plaques halt every leg, triangles grant priority, and slashed rings ban moves.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.question_text: What key action difference separates a stop sign from a yield sign?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.teaching_text: Every stop sign requires zero wheel roll, whereas a yield lets you ease through after slowing only if priority traffic is clear.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.question_text: What legal force do black-and-white regulatory signs carry, and what do flashing school-zone and disabled-parking signs require?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.teaching_text: Regulatory panels carry full statutory weight—slowing to the school limit while yellow flashes and reserving disabled stalls for plated or placarded cars.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.question_text: How do regulatory panels govern lane arrows, turn/vehicle bans, dividers, center turn lanes, ideal-weather speeds, and passing?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.teaching_text: White rectangles lock mandatory turn lanes, keep cars right of medians, limit center bays to left turns, and cap ideal-condition speeds.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.question_text: How does a single-movement lane-use sign differ from a dual-arrow optional lane panel beside it?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.teaching_text: An ONLY arrow forces every car in your lane to turn, whereas a straight-plus-turn arrow lets adjacent drivers pick either path.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.question_text: Which single maneuver is legal inside a shared center lane, and what maneuver is strictly banned?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.teaching_text: Treating the shared middle strip as a passing lane puts you nose-to-nose with oncoming drivers pulling in to turn left.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.question_text: What look and purpose define standard warning signs, and what roadway situations—from divided-road ends to deer and ending lanes—do they flag?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.teaching_text: Spotting a yellow diamond tells you to ease speed and scan ahead for curves, narrow bridges, steep grades, crossings, or lane drops.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.question_text: How does a Merge warning diamond differ from an Added Lane diamond in what entering drivers must do?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.teaching_text: Merging folds two streams into a single lane requiring gap matching, whereas an added lane gives incoming cars their own dedicated strip.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.question_text: What do night object reflectors, downward-sloping barricade stripes, and T-intersection diamonds each tell you?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.teaching_text: Reflectors outline bridge piers and culverts in the dark, downward stripes point to the safe open side, and T-signs mean your road dead-ends.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.question_text: How does the downward slant of diagonal barricade stripes tell you whether to pass left or right?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.teaching_text: Stripes sloping downward right guide your tires to the right, while stripes sloping downward left guide you cleanly left.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.question_text: Where do you halt for a train, which commercial/bus vehicles must stop at tracks by law, and when is passing them banned?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.teaching_text: Halt fifteen to fifty feet short for trains, and never pass mandatory-stopping school, church, coach, or hazmat rigs on two-lane roads.
sec04-card-sec04-F09.must_match_memory_hook: Fifteen to fifty feet, buses halt

visual_sync.text_span: Fifteen to fifty feet, buses halt

sec04-card-sec04-R07.question_text: How does your response at the round yellow railroad advance sign differ from your response at the trackside crossbuck?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.teaching_text: Round yellow alerts you early to drop speed for a fifteen-to-fifty-foot halt, while the white crossbuck sits right at the tracks demanding look-listen-yield.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.question_text: What rules apply at flashing rail lights, lowering crossing gates, and signed No Train Horn quiet zones?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.teaching_text: Never drive around gates before arms rise and lights stop—and at quiet zones, scan extra hard because trains skip routine horn blasts.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.question_text: When does it become legal to proceed at a flashing-light-only rail crossing versus a gated crossing?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.teaching_text: Second trains hide behind departing cabooses on multi-track lines, and gated crossings stay strictly illegal until arms lift and lights go dark.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.question_text: What color, shapes, channelizing gear, arrow boards, and speeding-fine multiplier govern Oklahoma highway work zones?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.teaching_text: Speeding fines double whenever crews or equipment occupy orange zones, so obey reduced speed caps and merge early with flashing arrows.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.question_text: How must you stop and proceed for a work-zone flagperson, and what fine and jail range hit drivers who ignore work-zone controls?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.teaching_text: Stay straight in your lane until waved forward—ignoring work-zone controls draws one hundred to one thousand dollars and up to thirty days jailed.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.question_text: How should you position your vehicle when halted by a flagperson, and what releases you to move forward?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.teaching_text: Swinging out of line around stopped cars puts you head-on into oncoming one-lane work traffic or exposed crew members.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.question_text: What job do cones, drums, and barricades handle, and what speed cap defines vehicles wearing the slow-moving-vehicle emblem?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.teaching_text: Spotting that reflective orange-red triangle ahead warns that a tractor or grader is crawling at twenty-five miles per hour or slower.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.question_text: How do Oklahoma guide colors, interstate milepost numbering directions, blue service panels, and highway litter barrels work?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.teaching_text: Interstate mileposts count upward from southern and western borders to pinpoint breakdowns, and highway trash belongs strictly inside rest-area or plaza barrels.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.question_text: What rules govern steady green, yellow, red, right-on-red, one-way left-on-red, and green arrows at Oklahoma intersections?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.teaching_text: After halting pre-crosswalk on red and yielding to pedestrians and bikes, drivers may turn right—or left one-way to one-way—unless banned.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.question_text: How do permitted movements differ across a steady red ball, a flashing red ball, and a flashing red arrow?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.teaching_text: Flashing red acts like a stop sign and steady red allows legal red turns, whereas a flashing red arrow bans turning until green.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.question_text: What do flashing yellow arrows, flashing yellow balls, crash-avoidance yielding on green, and vertical lens order establish?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.teaching_text: Flashing yellow arrows allow lefts after yielding, green never excuses hitting someone, and top-red middle-yellow bottom-green aids color-blind drivers.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.question_text: How do pedestrian figures, overhead lane-control lights, and yellow/white pavement stripes regulate crossings, reversible lanes, and passing?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.teaching_text: Pedestrians obey walk figures over car lights, overhead red X closes lanes while green opens, and solid yellow on your side bans passing.

sec04-card-sec04-R12.question_text: How do steady walk figures, flashing pedestrian figures, and steady red figures control stepping off or finishing a crosswalk?
sec04-card-sec04-R12.teaching_text: Stepping off the curb on a flashing countdown risks getting stranded mid-street when cross traffic gets green—only walkers already crossing finish.

sec04-card-sec04-R11.question_text: When do broken yellow, solid yellow on your side, and double solid yellow centerlines allow crossing?
sec04-card-sec04-R11.teaching_text: Solid yellow next to your lane blocks overtaking, and double solid yellow bars passing both ways while still permitting left-turn crossovers.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.question_text: How does Oklahoma treat right-of-way as a privilege, and when must even an entitled driver yield?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.teaching_text: Assuming legal entitlement shields your fenders causes intersection T-bones that eye contact and yielding prevent.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: May a driver claim right-of-way by force, or must entitled drivers yield when danger looms?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.teaching_text: Every permit check rewards drivers who surrender technical priority immediately whenever collision danger appears.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.question_text: Why do children near streets demand extreme caution, and which three places require slowing down?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.teaching_text: Kids bolt after balls or wobble unsignaled on bikes without checking oncoming traffic first.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.question_text: How does unpredictable child play shape your speed around schools, playgrounds, and residential blocks?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: Dropping speed early around homes and play areas buys stopping feet when children dart out.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.question_text: Which canes or animals identify a blind pedestrian in Oklahoma, and how far back must you stop?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.teaching_text: Halting fifteen feet short outside the crosswalk keeps blind pedestrians safe from crowding bumpers.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: Which three cane styles or guide animal trigger Oklahoma's fifteen-foot stop zone?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: All-white, red-tipped white, and chrome tapping canes each carry identical fifteen-foot right-of-way protection.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.question_text: When may an entire funeral procession clear an intersection regardless of signals, and how are cars marked?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.teaching_text: Once the lead car enters legally, cutting between lit headlights breaks Oklahoma funeral right-of-way.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.question_text: What unlocks intersection passage for a headlight-lit funeral line, and what is banned?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.teaching_text: Lit headlights warn cross-street traffic to hold steady until the final procession car clears.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.question_text: How do your stopping or slowing duties compare at unsigned highway entries, stop signs, and yield signs?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.teaching_text: Rolling past crosswalk lines at stop signs or charging through yield triangles triggers side-impact wrecks.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: How does the required action at a stop sign differ from a yield sign?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: Stop octagons demand full tire stillness before the crosswalk whereas yield triangles allow safe merges.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.question_text: At which types of crosswalks must Oklahoma drivers yield to pedestrians, and where is extra alertness needed?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.teaching_text: Missing paint lines at an intersection corner never cancels a pedestrian's crosswalk right-of-way.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.question_text: Who holds priority over a left-turning vehicle, and where must alley or driveway exits stop?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.teaching_text: Nosing out past a building onto the sidewalk traps joggers before you ever check street lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.question_text: What clears a left turn to go, and what line stops a private-driveway exit first?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.teaching_text: Misjudging oncoming speed on lefts and rolling across sidewalks from driveways top urban crash lists.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.question_text: Who goes first at a four-way stop or uncontrolled crossing, and how do ties break?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.teaching_text: When two bumpers halt together, the driver on the left always yields to the right.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.question_text: Which two short rules settle every arrival order at a four-way stop?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.teaching_text: Checking arrival order first and looking right on ties prevents awkward four-corner standoffs.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.question_text: How should you scan, pace, accelerate, and handle gridlock when crossing an intersection?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.teaching_text: Braking mid-turn invites rear-end strikes while entering backed-up lanes strands your tail across cross traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.question_text: What scanning sequence opens an intersection entry, and how do your pedals clear it?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.teaching_text: Left-side cross traffic reaches your driver door first, making that second left glance essential.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.question_text: How must you yield to flashing or siren emergency vehicles versus unlit ones or stopped roadside cars?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.teaching_text: Even from the left lane, signaled stops go right while hazard-lit shoulder cars earn space.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.question_text: How do signaled emergency rigs, silent unlit rigs, and roadside vehicles differ in right-of-way?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.teaching_text: Cruising ambulances without lights flow like regular traffic whereas flashing responders command immediate right-edge clearance.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.question_text: When may you pass a red-flashing school bus, which roads excuse stopping, and what penalty hits violators?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.teaching_text: Blowing past a boarding school bus endangers children and triggers a mandatory one-year license revocation.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.question_text: Which three signals end a school-bus stop, and which three road layouts excuse stopping?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.teaching_text: Oncoming lanes on a divided highway need not stop, yet undivided two-way lanes always halt.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.question_text: How does Oklahoma's Move Over Law differ for multi-lane highways versus two-lane roads?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.teaching_text: Distracted drivers drifting into flashing shoulder units cause deadly secondary crashes that buffer lanes prevent.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.question_text: What action satisfies the Move Over Law on a multi-lane road compared with a two-lane road?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.teaching_text: Multi-lane drivers open an empty lane when safe while two-lane drivers drop speed cautiously.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.question_text: What is a Traffic Incident Management scene, and which five habits protect responders inside it?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.teaching_text: Gawking at crash wreckage pulls your eyes off warning cones and braking bumpers ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.question_text: Which four driver behaviors keep Traffic Incident Management zones safe from secondary pileups?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.teaching_text: Passing advance-warning and transition cones smoothly with zero rubbernecking shields crews working inches from traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: How do dashed and solid yellow lines differ from dashed and solid white lane lines?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Confusing yellow and white stripes risks turning into oncoming traffic on a two-way street.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: Which stripe color separates opposing directions, and how does solid yellow differ from dashed?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Solid yellow bans overtaking oncoming lanes while still letting drivers turn left across safely.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: How do center markings and rules change across two-lane, three-lane, and four-lane roadways?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Using a shared three-lane center turn strip as an overtaking lane causes head-on wrecks.
sec06-card-sec06-F02.must_match_memory_hook: Two passes, three turns, four seals

visual_sync.text_span: Two passes, three turns, four seals

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: What does the center of the road allow on two-lane, three-lane, and four-lane streets?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Reading center stripes instantly tells you whether passing, shared left turns, or zero crossing applies.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: What check sequence makes a lane change safe, and how do you treat a signaling leader?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Mirrors alone miss cars riding off your rear quarter panel without a quick shoulder glance.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: In what order do safe lane-change checks run before you move sideways?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Skipping any link in the check chain or lingering in blind spots invites sideswipe crashes.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: What design defines a limited-access expressway, and what minimum and maximum speeds govern it?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Crawling below forty miles per hour on clear expressways creates closing-speed hazards and breaks law.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: Between what speed floor and ceiling range do Oklahoma expressways run, and is crawling legal?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: Underpowered vehicles unable to hold the forty-mile-per-hour minimum stay barred from limited-access ramps.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: Which expressway lanes belong to slower versus faster traffic, and which three habits violate discipline?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Lane-hopping saves almost zero trip time while boxing neighbors inside tight highway packs.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: Alongside keeping slower traffic right, which three multi-lane habits break Oklahoma expressway rules?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Holding one centered lane outside neighbors' blind spots keeps escape space open on every side.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: How many seconds should you follow and scan ahead on expressways, and how do you handle missed exits?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Backing up on shoulders or cutting across grassy medians causes fatal high-speed expressway T-bones.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: What following count, forward scan window, and missed-exit fix govern expressway travel?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Scanning fifteen to twenty seconds downroad spots brake waves early while next-exit loops fix wrong turns.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: Who yields when entering an expressway, and how do you use the acceleration lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Stopping dead at the end of an acceleration ramp leaves zero speed to merge safely.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: When do you signal and slow down for an expressway exit ramp?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Braking hard in live highway lanes before entering the deceleration ramp triggers high-speed rear-enders.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: How does speed handling in an expressway entry lane contrast with an exit ramp?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: Highway velocitization tricks exiting drivers into carrying dangerous speed into tight off-ramp curves.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: Where must an expressway breakdown pull off, and where must passengers and pedestrians stay?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Walking along high-speed expressway edges exposes stranded motorists to seventy-mile-per-hour mirror strikes.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: What shoulder position, lighting, and foot-traffic rule govern forced expressway stops?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Clearing travel lanes completely and keeping everyone away from asphalt edges prevents roadside tragedy.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: When is camping in the left lane illegal on four-lane highways, and may you speed to pass?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Passing another car never grants legal permission to push the speedometer above posted limits.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.question_text: What left-lane habit breaks wide-road law, and does overtaking excuse breaking the speed limit?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.teaching_text: Drivers often assume quick bursts above the posted cap are legal while overtaking slower traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: How much clear road ahead does a left pass need, and when may you pull back right?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Cutting right before spotting both headlights of the passed car in your mirror clips bumpers.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.question_text: Which three clearance checks anchor a clean left-side pass from start to return?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.teaching_text: Checking your left blind spot first catches trailing cars that already started passing you.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: Under which three conditions is passing on the right legal, and where are no-passing zones set?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Passing on unpaved shoulders or within one hundred feet of bridges, rails, or intersections invites head-ons.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.question_text: Which three road setups allow right-side passing, and what shortcut is always illegal?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.teaching_text: Dropping tires onto gravel or paved shoulders to sneak past a left-turning car breaks law.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: How must a driver being passed cooperate, especially if oncoming traffic closes in?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Accelerating to block an overtaking car traps both vehicles in a lethal head-on squeeze.

sec06-card-sec06-R12.question_text: Which four blind zones forbid passing, and how must an overtaken driver assist?
sec06-card-sec06-R12.teaching_text: Solid stripes, crests, curves, and hundred-foot bridge or rail approaches hide oncoming traffic completely.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: How far ahead must turn signals start, and how do left-arm hand signals point?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Signaling at least one hundred feet or one-third block early gives followers braking room.

sec06-card-sec06-R13.question_text: What distance starts a legal turn signal, and which three left-arm angles signal moves?
sec06-card-sec06-R13.teaching_text: Pulling your signaling arm back inside before turning lets both hands steer cleanly around corners.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: When do you brake versus accelerate for a turn, and how must wheels point before turning left?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Pre-turning front wheels left lets a rear-end bump shove your car straight into oncoming lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-R14.question_text: How do braking, gentle throttle, and wheel aim work together in Oklahoma's six-step turn?
sec06-card-sec06-R14.teaching_text: Finishing braking before the crosswalk keeps tires planted as gentle acceleration carries through the corner.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.question_text: How do you position and finish a five-step left turn, and how do opposing left-turners pass?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.teaching_text: Passing in front of an opposing left-turner rather than behind keeps sightlines open both ways.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.question_text: How should you position your car for a right turn, and what top speed applies?
