sec12-card-sec12-R03.question_text: What is the cruel order in which alcohol strips away a driver's mental faculties and physical senses?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.teaching_text: Waiting until you feel drunk to hand over your keys fails because honest self-assessment disappears first.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.question_text: Which three serving sizes of beer, wine, and eighty-proof liquor carry the exact same pure alcohol?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.teaching_text: Switching from liquor shots to cans of beer delivers identical bloodstream ethanol ounce for standard serving.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.question_text: Why doesn't choosing wine or beer over mixed cocktails reduce your blood-alcohol dose?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.teaching_text: Your liver processes pure ethanol molecules identically regardless of carbonation, grape juice, or glass shape.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.question_text: How do pep pills, medical marijuana, and amphetamines affect Oklahoma driving legality and crash risk?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.teaching_text: Holding a state medical dispensary card gives zero immunity behind the wheel if any cannabis trace shows up.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.question_text: Who helps verify prescription safety before driving, and how do cannabis and street stimulants compare with alcohol?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.teaching_text: Warning stickers on pill bottles exist because legal prescriptions can wreck lane tracking worse than booze.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.question_text: What blood-alcohol range defines Oklahoma's impaired-driving offense below point-oh-eight, and what penalties apply?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.teaching_text: Blowing under point-oh-eight is never a free pass when Oklahoma prosecutes lower blood-alcohol impairment with jail time.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.question_text: What criminal exposure hits an Oklahoma driver convicted with blood alcohol between point-oh-five and point-oh-eight?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.teaching_text: Many drivers wrongly think anything below point-oh-eight is legal until a misdemeanor sentence hits their record.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.question_text: What triggers implied consent to chemical testing in Oklahoma, and what happens if you refuse or fail?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.teaching_text: Even sitting parked with keys in physical control triggers automatic administrative revocation if you decline the breathalyzer.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.question_text: Why does refusing a roadside chemical test cost your license even if you are completely sober?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.teaching_text: Administrative license revocation runs separately from criminal court the moment a test is refused or failed.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.question_text: Can an Oklahoma officer prove impairment without a chemical test, and what substances count toward DUI?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.teaching_text: Slurred speech, glassy eyes, and weaving lanes establish criminal intoxication whether caused by liquor, pills, or both.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.question_text: Why doesn't beating or skipping a breathalyzer protect an impaired driver from a DUI conviction?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.teaching_text: Dashcam footage and trained roadside testimony carry full evidentiary weight across every intoxicating substance.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.question_text: What three suspension lengths follow first, second, and third conviction notices?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.teaching_text: Each repeat conviction notice multiplies your time off the road until routine commuting becomes impossible.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.question_text: How does suspension length escalate across three successive conviction notices?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.teaching_text: Repeat offenders lose months and eventually an entire calendar year of legal driving privileges.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.question_text: How do jail terms, fines, and felony status escalate from a first point-oh-eight DUI to repeat offenses?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.teaching_text: Notice Oklahoma pairs jail AND fines together and upgrades a second offense within ten years into a state felony.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.question_text: How quickly does Oklahoma's DUI criminal ladder jump from county jail days to state prison years?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.teaching_text: Unlike states that keep second DUIs as misdemeanors, Oklahoma attaches a lifelong felony tag inside a ten-year window.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.question_text: What license revocation lengths apply to first, second, and third DUI convictions within ten years?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.teaching_text: Oklahoma prevents double-stacking only when the exact same stop already triggered an implied-consent revocation.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.question_text: How do prior ten-year revocations stretch your license loss after a DUI conviction?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.teaching_text: Prior alcohol entries stay active on your ten-year lookback window and double each revocation tier.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.question_text: Beyond court fines, what financial, career, and college consequences pile onto an alcohol arrest?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.teaching_text: Ignition interlock leases, high-risk insurance rates, and felony background checks follow young drivers long after probation ends.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.question_text: Which seven everyday areas take a hit after an impaired-driving arrest?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.teaching_text: A twenty-dollar rideshare home costs pennies next to thousands in legal retainers, breath interlocks, and lost aid.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.question_text: What triggers Oklahoma's zero-tolerance law for drivers under twenty-one, and how long are licenses revoked?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.teaching_text: Even a tiny sip registering on a breath machine strips a teen's license for months on a first stop.

sec12-card-sec12-R13.question_text: Which three substance categories violate zero tolerance for any driver under twenty-one?
sec12-card-sec12-R13.teaching_text: Adult blood-alcohol thresholds never apply before your twenty-first birthday anywhere on Oklahoma roads.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.question_text: What fines apply to youth zero-tolerance offenses, and what happens when someone under eighteen commits any alcohol or drug offense?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.teaching_text: Notice an under-eighteen substance offense doesn't even need a car involved to cancel driving privileges up to twenty-one.

sec12-card-sec12-R14.question_text: How can judges substitute youth fines, and who automatically learns about every under-eighteen substance conviction?
sec12-card-sec12-R14.teaching_text: Party citations far from any parking lot still land directly on Service Oklahoma's desk and pull teen licenses.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: Who counts as a pedestrian in Oklahoma, how do crosswalks work, and how must drivers treat jaywalkers?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Even when someone steps mid-block outside painted lines, steel yields to flesh to prevent an irreversible tragedy.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: Which road users hold priority in both marked and unmarked crosswalks, and what if someone crosses elsewhere?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Winning a right-of-way argument never excuses striking an exposed person on foot or wheels.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: How do you protect blind pedestrians, sidewalk users, and walkers hidden from adjacent lanes by your stopped car?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Revving an engine panics crossing seniors, while flashing brake lamps alerts overtakers in the next lane to stop too.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: Which groups require unhurried yielding, and how can your brake pedal protect someone crossing ahead of your hood?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: A distracted driver in the adjacent lane sees your pulsing red taillights long before spotting a child ahead.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: What road rights do Oklahoma bicyclists hold, why might they swerve suddenly, and what passing clearance does law require?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Skinny tires dodge storm grates, loose dogs, and swinging car doors instantly without time for a hand signal.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: Why must drivers anticipate sudden bicycle movement and hold wide statutory clearance?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Cutting back right too early clips a front bicycle wheel before your rear bumper clears the handlebars.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: How should you pass a cyclist on two-lane or narrow streets, use your horn, and set up right turns?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Blasting an air-horn startles a young rider sideways, and turning right from the left of a bike causes right-hooks.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.question_text: Which four habits prevent collisions when overtaking or turning near a bicyclist?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.teaching_text: Patience on tight residential blocks costs five seconds while preventing irreversible handlebar sideswipes.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: When may an Oklahoma cyclist legally take the full travel lane instead of riding near the right edge?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Honking at a rider centered in a narrow or obstacle-lined lane misunderstands Oklahoma traffic law completely.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.question_text: Which four situations allow a bicyclist to ride in the center of the lane?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.teaching_text: Giving riders full lane command through pinch points stops cars from attempting dangerous same-lane squeezes.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: How does Oklahoma law distinguish a bicyclist's duty at a stop sign from a red traffic light?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Oklahoma allows cautious momentum through clear stop-sign intersections while keeping full stops mandatory on red bulbs.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.question_text: What is the key difference between stop signs and red lights for cyclists under Oklahoma law?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.teaching_text: Drivers knowing this rule will not be surprised when a yielding cyclist rolls smoothly past an empty stop sign.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: What causes most car-motorcycle crashes, what lane space do riders own, and what credential is required?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Human brains wired to scan for wide grilles look straight past a slim single headlight approaching at full speed.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.question_text: Why do cars collide with motorcycles so often, and what legal status protects riders?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.teaching_text: Never crowd beside a motorcycle just because open asphalt shows on one side of its tires.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: How should you pass, follow, check blind spots, and read lane-position shifts around a motorcycle?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: Riders slide across their lane deliberately to escape blind zones, dodge oil slicks, and see past tall traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.question_text: Which four habits keep motorcycles safe when you trail behind or overtake them?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.teaching_text: Close high-speed passes buffet light two-wheelers sideways with bow-wave air pressure from your front bumper.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: What extra care applies around motorcycles in bad weather or darkness, and what eye protection does statute require?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Slick asphalt steals two-wheel braking traction while a single insect strike at highway speed blinds an unprotected rider.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.question_text: How do intersections, night driving, and rider face protection each work around motorcycles?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.teaching_text: A lone motorcycle taillight blends into distant traffic unless following drivers drop high beams promptly.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: How big are a heavy truck's front, side, and rear blind spots, and how should you stop behind one uphill?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Stopping back and slightly left on grades keeps your hood clear of clutch rollback and visible in the cab mirror.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.question_text: Where do smart drivers stay positioned behind and uphill of heavy freight trucks?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.teaching_text: If your windshield cannot spot the trucker's side mirror, fifty tons of freight has zero idea you are there.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: How do you signal, complete, and cooperate on passes with heavy trucks, and how do you meet oncoming rigs?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: Cutting back in and tapping brakes on a downhill grade forces heavy trailers onto hot air brakes instantly.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.question_text: What three rules govern announcing a truck pass, finishing on downgrades, and meeting rigs head-on?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.teaching_text: Air turbulence between opposing vehicles actually pushes cars outward rather than sucking them inward toward the trailer.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.question_text: Which two spaces around turning or reversing trucks must a driver never enter?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.teaching_text: Trailers swing left only to pivot right rear tandems straight across the curb lane where impatient cars sneak in.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.question_text: What must you never try beside a wide-turning truck or behind a backing rig?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.teaching_text: Thirty seconds of patience while a tractor backs into a bay beats getting pinned inside a total blind zone.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: How far does a highway-speed train need to stop, who is at fault in rail crashes, and when do most happen?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: Familiar neighborhood crossings in bright daylight breed fatal complacency when drivers gamble over a ninety-second wait.

sec10-card-sec10-R13.question_text: Why do locomotives always hold absolute right of way over motor vehicles?
sec10-card-sec10-R13.teaching_text: Steel wheels carry thousands of tons that physically cannot halt inside human sight distance.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.question_text: Between what exact distances must you halt at railroad tracks, and which four warnings trigger that stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.teaching_text: Oklahoma sets both an outer fifty-foot limit and an inner fifteen-foot buffer whenever horns, lamps, gates, or trains warn.

sec10-card-sec10-R14.question_text: What stopping window and four hazard cues govern railroad approaches in Oklahoma?
sec10-card-sec10-R14.teaching_text: Memorizing both ends of Oklahoma's rail stopping zone locks down a classic numeric permit-test favorite.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.question_text: How do advance signs, R-X-R paint, crossbucks, red flashers, gates, and stop signs each work at tracks?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.teaching_text: Treating bare white crossbucks like active yield signs ensures you scan numbered multi-track crossings even without gates.

sec10-card-sec10-R15.question_text: Which six roadside and pavement devices build the warning chain at a railroad crossing?
sec10-card-sec10-R15.teaching_text: From the first yellow disk down to drop arms, each marker gives earlier chances to shed speed smoothly.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.question_text: What rules prevent getting trapped on tracks, what if gates drop behind you, and how do you escape a stall?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.teaching_text: Crossing gates are engineered not to trap exiting cars, and twenty seconds from first flash leaves zero time to restart.

sec10-card-sec10-R16.question_text: Which four survival rules cover clearing tracks, crossing gates, stalled evacuations, and emergency calls?
sec10-card-sec10-R16.teaching_text: Running forty-five degrees toward the oncoming locomotive keeps you clear of wreckage flung downrange on impact.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.question_text: Which vehicles halt at every rail crossing, why is passing banned there, and why do eyes misread train speed?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.teaching_text: Large objects appear to move deceptively slowly, and rail grooves can catch bicycle tires mid-crossing.

sec10-card-sec10-R17.question_text: Who stops routinely at tracks, who is barred from passing, and what visual illusion fools drivers?
sec10-card-sec10-R17.teaching_text: Expecting church buses, school buses, and fuel tankers to brake at silent rails prevents sudden rear-end collisions.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.question_text: What slow vehicles travel rural Oklahoma roads, what rights do animal-drawn carts hold, and what marks sub-twenty-five rigs?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.teaching_text: Cresting a blind county hill at highway pace closes the gap on a wide combine harvester in seconds.

sec10-card-sec10-R18.question_text: How fast do farm and maintenance crawlers move, how are animal rigs treated, and what symbol warns you?
sec10-card-sec10-R18.teaching_text: Spotting the reflective orange-and-red triangle early lets you shed forty miles per hour smoothly without skidding.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.question_text: Can you apply for a new license or drive legally while suspended or revoked, and how does Oklahoma treat violators?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.teaching_text: Getting pulled over before completing official reinstatement turns an administrative hold into a harsh criminal charge.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.question_text: Which two actions remain completely off-limits until a suspended or revoked license is formally restored?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.teaching_text: Even after your calendar wait expires, driving stays illegal until reinstatement steps clear your file.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.question_text: Who legally owns your Oklahoma driver license, and what types of misuse or alteration cancel it?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.teaching_text: Loaning your plastic ID to a friend or altering a birth digit destroys your own valid driving privilege.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.question_text: Whose property is an Oklahoma credential, and how many statutory misuse paths trigger cancellation?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.teaching_text: Identity-verification scanners catch borrowed photos, forged names, and altered dates instantly at counters and stops.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.question_text: What felony prison and fine maximums hit fake-ID buyers or carriers, and when do license examiners commit a felony?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.teaching_text: Buying a novelty fake ID online for weekend concerts carries state-prison felony exposure in Oklahoma.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.question_text: How does Oklahoma punish someone carrying or borrowing a fake ID versus a corrupt issuer who helps create one?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.teaching_text: Oklahoma closes both ends of credential fraud by charging buyers, borrowers, and dishonest counter staff with felonies.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.question_text: Which crashes and court convictions land on your Service Oklahoma driving record, and what happens if you move states?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.teaching_text: Out-of-state speeding tickets follow you home electronically, and moving away sends your full file to your new DMV.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.question_text: Why doesn't getting a ticket across state lines or moving out of Oklahoma wipe your driving history clean?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.teaching_text: National driver registries link state agencies so convictions and qualifying wrecks travel wherever you apply.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.question_text: How can you request a three-year Oklahoma driving summary, what fee applies, and who gets it free?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.teaching_text: Checking your three-year abstract before shopping auto insurance catches clerical errors and verifies clean discounts.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.question_text: What is the standard price of a three-year driving record, and which age group pays nothing?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.teaching_text: Memorizing both the standard dollar fee and the senior exemption handles quick administrative exam items.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.question_text: Who gets called into a compliance hearing or medical review, what do safety courses teach, and what if habits stay unsafe?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.teaching_text: Compliance interventions offer structured coaching to fix risky habits before a preventable crash forces revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.question_text: What is the goal of a driver compliance hearing, and what happens when a driver fails to improve?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.teaching_text: Public road safety comes first whenever coaching and medical standards cannot restore safe vehicle control.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.question_text: How does Oklahoma classify every driver license held under age eighteen, and how many moving violations can trigger suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.teaching_text: Adults get ten points of cushion, whereas a single speeding ticket lets the state suspend a minor's license.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.question_text: Why must drivers under eighteen treat their license like an active trial period?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.teaching_text: Discretionary suspension authority means teen drivers never have spare points to burn on careless tickets.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.question_text: Which seven serious conviction categories trigger mandatory Oklahoma revocation, and what is the revocation window?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.teaching_text: Major offenses bypass the point table completely and pull your license immediately on conviction.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.question_text: How long do Oklahoma's seven mandatory-revocation offenses pull privileges, and how are same-incident alcohol revocations handled?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.teaching_text: One single DUI stop will not stack two separate revocations if implied consent already pulled your card.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.question_text: Where does every driver's point balance start, and what point total within what timeframe triggers suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.teaching_text: Every driver starts at zero, so keeping clean habits preserves a wide buffer against administrative suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.question_text: What cumulative score and lookback window suspend an Oklahoma license under the point system?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.teaching_text: Multiple minor citations across several years add up quietly until one last two-point stop crosses the threshold.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.question_text: Which violations add four, three, two, or one point on Oklahoma's point schedule?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.teaching_text: Notice passing a flashing school bus matches reckless driving at the very top of Oklahoma's point chart.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.question_text: Which two violations sit at the four-point top of the point chart, and which sit at the one-point bottom?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.teaching_text: Just two school-bus or reckless convictions put you one ordinary ticket away from losing your license.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.question_text: How do clean twelve-month stretches, three clean years, and defensive-driving courses reduce your Oklahoma point total?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.teaching_text: Notice you cannot bank negative credit below zero ahead of future tickets, though three spotless years wipe any balance clean.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.question_text: Which two paths subtract points from your driving record, and why can't you bank negative points?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.teaching_text: Taking an approved defensive course shaves active points off a bruised record while building safer traffic instincts.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.question_text: What are Oklahoma's mandatory liability insurance minimums, who can demand proof, and what penalties hit uninsured drivers?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.teaching_text: Failing to update a moved mailing address can leave you driving on an unknowing insurance suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-R12.question_text: Which four reminders wrap up Oklahoma's compulsory insurance and licensing chapter?
sec13-card-sec13-R12.teaching_text: Uninsured tickets hit three ways at once with cash fines, county jail exposure, and suspended tags and license.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.question_text: What three vehicle credentials belong with a driven Oklahoma car, where do you handle them, and what sets title-transfer fees?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.teaching_text: Paying taxes and fees at Service Oklahoma or a licensed operator earns your plate or sticker, while sales require transferring title.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.question_text: How does what vehicle registration proves differ from what a title transfer proves?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.teaching_text: Your annual plate sticker shows road taxes are current, whereas the signed title document establishes legal ownership at a sale.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.question_text: Where does Service Oklahoma mail every official notice, and how can an outdated address cost your license?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.teaching_text: Letters go strictly to your address on file, meaning an unreported move can leave your license suspended without you realizing.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.question_text: Why does failing to update your Service Oklahoma mailing address create a hidden suspension hazard?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.teaching_text: State mail never hunts down new apartments—missing an unanswered deadline sent to your old address suspends privileges quietly.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.question_text: What does vehicle liability mean, and what three dollar minimums per accident does the Oklahoma manual print?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.teaching_text: Liability covers financial fault for crash harm, printed on Oklahoma's compulsory page as twenty-five thousand, fifty thousand, and twenty-five thousand property.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.question_text: How are all three of Oklahoma's printed $25,000 / $50,000 / $25,000 compulsory liability minimums measured?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.teaching_text: Each separate collision resets your policy's twenty-five-thousand, fifty-thousand, and twenty-five-thousand property coverage caps.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.question_text: What insurance form must stay in your car, who can demand to inspect it, and what three details should you copy after a crash?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.teaching_text: Keep an owner or non-owner verification form handy for officers, staff, and crash parties, recording their full name, license number, and birth date.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.question_text: Which three groups have the right to see your insurance verification form, and what do you record at a collision?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.teaching_text: Sharing verification works both ways at a wreck—show your form promptly and write down the other driver's identifying info.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.question_text: What injury or dollar-damage threshold suspends uninsured crash drivers and owners, and what does a court-reported no-proof ticket suspend?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.teaching_text: Crashing uninsured with bodily injury or five hundred dollars in damage suspends your license, while no-proof tickets suspend tags too.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.question_text: How does the suspension triggered by an uninsured crash differ from a court-reported no-proof traffic ticket?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.teaching_text: Uninsured wrecks pull driving privileges directly, whereas failing to show proof on a stop prompts courts to suspend registration plates too.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.question_text: What fine, jail time, and credential losses follow a conviction for driving uninsured or refusing to show proof?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.teaching_text: Conviction carries up to two hundred fifty dollars, up to thirty days jailed, or both—plus losing both license and registration.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.question_text: How does Oklahoma classify forging a security verification form versus merely possessing a fake one, and whose forms count?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.teaching_text: Making fake proof is a felony and carrying one brings a two-hundred-fifty-dollar misdemeanor plus mandatory suspension—always verify borrowed cars first.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.question_text: What criminal grade separates manufacturing a fake Oklahoma insurance form from simply keeping one in your glovebox?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.teaching_text: Even if someone else printed the phony card, holding it draws up to two hundred fifty dollars and mandatory license-and-tag suspension.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.question_text: Which occupants must wear federally approved factory seat belts in Oklahoma, and how do belts protect them?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.teaching_text: Fastened belts cushion cabin impacts, keep drivers anchored at the wheel, and stop riders from flying forward or out.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.question_text: What three physical crash protections do fastened seat belts deliver to riders?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.teaching_text: Spreading crash energy keeps you conscious behind the controls instead of slamming the glass or flying onto pavement.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.question_text: What restraint rules govern Oklahoma children under 2, under 8, and aged 4 to 8 up to 4 feet 9 inches?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.teaching_text: Kids stay rear-facing until age two or maker caps and restrained under eight, with four-to-eight riders up to four-foot-nine using a restraint or belt.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.question_text: How do Oklahoma's child-restraint rules shift across age 2, ages 4 to 8, and height 4 feet 9 inches?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.teaching_text: Turning two opens forward-facing seats once maker limits allow, and ages four through eight at or below four-foot-nine use restraints or belts.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.question_text: Why must children never ride loose or in front of airbags, who belongs in back, and how much safer is the rear seat?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.teaching_text: Airbags have killed riders under five feet tall and adult arms cannot hold infants, making the back row at least twenty-six percent safer.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.question_text: Why does holding a baby in an adult's arms or letting kids stand on seats or floorboards turn deadly?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.teaching_text: Sudden crash deceleration rips an unrestrained infant straight toward the windshield and throws standing kids headfirst into trim.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.question_text: Which two groups under 5 feet tall have suffered fatal airbag injuries, where should under-12s sit, and what is the rear-seat safety gain?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.teaching_text: Explosive passenger airbags threaten small children and shorter older adults alike, whereas riding in back cuts injury risk at least twenty-six percent.
